title: keyboard-first-resize-and-sticky-aggregates-for-high-density-virtual-tables
creator: Alex Kim
description: Design a refinement of the table component for the Console that enables keyboard-first column resizing, an optional sticky aggregates row/column (for sums, medians, custom rollups), and a density token layer that supports very high-density telemetry tables (e.g., token-level cost breakdowns). Goals: preserve virtualization performance, keep single-row height variants, and maintain a11y focus order and announcement semantics.
rationale: Console customers are increasingly using tables with hundreds of rows and many columns (cost breakdowns, per-token traces). Current resizing is mouse-only and aggregate values vanish when scrolled. Engineering requests a design that keeps DOM footprint low (virtualization) while exposing helpful data (sticky aggregates) and making resizing accessible via keyboard for keyboard-only and screen-reader users.
acceptance_criteria: Column resize: keyboard controls (Enter to activate, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight to resize in small increments, Shift+Arrows for larger jumps, Esc to cancel) documented and implemented in prototype
Sticky aggregates: optional feature toggle per table instance; sticky row/column must not break virtualization (aggregates rendered in separate sticky layer)
Density tokens: three modes (compact, standard, spacious) implemented in examples and token values added to Design System token page
Sorting/filtering: multi-column inline filter strip supports keyboard navigation and announces filter state to SR; persisted filter chips in header
Performance: scrolling benchmarks show no >10% increase in frame time for 10k rows compared to baseline virtual table without aggregates
Visual QA: Focus ring and contrast meet WCAG 2.1 AA for all interactive controls
Docs: Figma spec, Confluence PRD, and example Storybook stories exist and linked from this ticket
prototyping_notes: Built a keyboard-enabled prototype in Storybook using a small JS harness that simulates virtualization by rendering only visible rows. For sticky aggregates, we layered a separate sticky container that mirrors column widths; syncing is done via resize observers in the prototype. Prototype revealed jitter when resize events fire rapidly — engineering asked for debounce and width snap heuristics.
tradeoffs: 1) Sticky aggregates as a separate layer keeps virtualization intact but requires width sync complexity. 2) Integrating aggregates into the virtual DOM simplifies sync but increases rendered node count for large row counts. We are pursuing separate sticky layer + width-snap to minimize nodes. 3) Keyboard resize adds more event handling complexity and must be throttled to avoid layout thrash.
decision: Proceed with separate sticky aggregates layer + width-snap heuristic (5px snap) + keyboard-first resize API. Implementation will expose an opt-in prop on the Table component to enable aggregates to avoid default performance impact.
accessibility_considerations: Keyboard entry point, focus management, ARIA live region announcements for resize start/stop and filter state, explicit labels for aggregate cells, ensure color tokens used for density modes meet contrast. Testing with NVDA/JAWS and VoiceOver required.
testing_plan: 1) Manual a11y pass with screen readers; 2) Performance regression test (10k rows) on staging; 3) Cross-browser check for sticky layering; 4) Unit tests for keyboard handlers and snap behavior; 5) UX validation with 3 internal PMs using an interactive prototype.
